c01s03.title: From ambition to an observable action
items: Who, when and through which route?
c01s03.caption: A fictional service example; a click is not the whole public benefit.

c01s03b.title: Three questions before a message
items: Can the person understand and perform the action?
Do time, resources and access permit it?
c01s03b.caption: The framework organizes hypotheses; it does not establish which one is correct.

c01s04.title: Two possible investigations
c01s04.caption: The example illustrates an investigation, not a finding about café visitors.

c01s05.title: A diagnosis before a solution
c01s05.caption: A framework supports questions rather than replacing an investigation.

c02s03.title: The work behind a booking
items: Submit and confirm a suitable appointment
c02s03.caption: This fictional journey includes work that a simple click count could miss.

c02s03b.title: Ask whose effort is counted
items: What must someone find or provide?
Who bears time, stress and expense?
c02s03b.caption: A process can become easier on average while leaving some people behind.

c02s04.title: Different changes, different barriers
left: Less effort in the booking route
c02s04.caption: Either change needs evidence about the barrier and the resulting service outcome.

c02s05.title: Assess a proposed simplification
items: Which costs change, and for whom?
Can people obtain a useful service?
c02s05.caption: Count consequences beyond the easiest-to-measure step.

c03s03.title: A message has several hurdles
items: Can the person do it now?
c03s03.caption: Failure at one hurdle does not establish failure at all the others.

c03s03b.title: Design a useful reminder
items: Can they change or stop messages?
c03s03b.caption: More messages can add burden without improving the intended outcome.

c03s04.title: Two measures with different jobs
c03s04.caption: Both can be useful; they answer different questions.

c03s05.title: A reminder hypothesis
items: One useful cue at a feasible moment
Compare meaningful action and unwanted costs
c03s05.caption: The figure is a proposed mechanism, not proof that the reminder will work.

c04s03.title: Presentation or a different offer?
c04s03.caption: Keep facts complete when comparing descriptions.

c04s03b.title: Interpreting default uptake
c04s03b.caption: A choice rate does not reveal a unique psychological mechanism.

c04s04.title: Review a default
items: Are terms clear before the choice?
Can people choose and change easily?
Who benefits or bears an unwanted cost?
c04s04.caption: Assess the process and its consequences together.

c04s05.title: Judge a choice design
c04s05.caption: A desirable-looking choice rate is not sufficient evidence of benefit.

c05s03.title: Two possible reasons for delay
c05s03.caption: Similar delays do not establish identical causes.

c05s03b.title: A feasible if-then plan
items: Can I actually carry out this step?
c05s03b.caption: A planning aid supports an intention; it does not remove every constraint.

c05s04.title: Review a planning aid
items: What could make the plan infeasible?
Can the arrangement be revised fairly?
c05s04.caption: Support for follow-through should not become punishment for uncertainty.

c05s05.title: From intention to an acceptable aid
items: The person’s chosen goal and barrier
A cue linked to a feasible response
c05s05.caption: A planning aid is conditional support, not proof of a motivational diagnosis.

c06s03.title: Two different norm claims
c06s03.caption: A message can contain either or both claims; truth and relevance still matter.

c06s03b.title: An average can have different meanings
items: Who changes, and in which direction?
c06s03b.caption: A group average can conceal different responses.

c06s04.title: Before publishing a norm claim
items: Which group and circumstances are meant?
c06s04.caption: Norm language does not remove the need for practical access or an outcome comparison.

c06s05.title: Evaluate the whole norm proposal
items: Who benefits or changes in an unwanted direction?
c06s05.caption: A fictional message illustrates questions to test, not an established intervention effect.

c07s03.title: Two proposals with different purposes
right: Effort may shift toward that result
c07s03.caption: Identify the purpose and likely costs before choosing an evaluation.

c07s03b.title: Follow the incentive beyond the count
items: More effort or different case selection
c07s03b.caption: The figure shows competing hypotheses, not a claim about volunteers’ motives.

c07s04.title: Review an incentive
items: Who can participate and who bears costs?
c07s04.caption: Fair compensation and a poorly designed performance target are different questions.

c07s05.title: An incentive evaluation
items: Access, effort or a specified result?
Benefit, quality, cost and fair access
c07s05.caption: Measure what matters beyond the easiest count.

c08s03.title: A reminder theory of change
items: A clear cue before the appointment
c08s03.caption: Assumptions include access, understanding and available service capacity.

c08s03b.title: Support a decision in different ways
c08s03b.caption: Material provision may also be needed; these are not the only intervention categories.

c08s04.title: Questions before a pilot
items: Does the proposal address the investigated barrier?
Can people implement and use it?
What comparison and outcomes are needed?
c08s04.caption: A good-looking prototype is not a causal result.

c08s05.title: From diagnosis to an evaluable proposal
items: Which outcomes and comparisons distinguish proposals?
c08s05.caption: Useful design includes the possibility that a behavioural message is not the best response.

c09s03.title: Two comparisons
right: Compare approaches in the same period
c09s03.caption: Design and implementation still matter; random assignment is not a guarantee of perfect evidence.

c09s03b.title: Illustrative attendance data
c09s03b.caption: Invented teaching numbers, not a research finding; they do not show uncertainty or transferability.

c09s04.title: Before interpreting a difference
c09s04.caption: An experiment is an argument supported by design and measurement, not just a positive number.

c09s05.title: A credible field comparison
items: Assignment, measurement and a recorded plan
c09s05.caption: A positive difference needs a defensible design and a bounded interpretation.

c10s03.title: Beyond the overall average
items: What else could these resources support?
c10s03.caption: A result informs a decision; it does not remove the need for a fairness judgment.

c10s03b.title: Rights are part of the design
c10s03b.caption: The specific legal and ethical requirements depend on the setting and need appropriate review.

c10s04.title: An expansion decision
items: What worked, for whom and under which conditions?
What differs in the new service?
Monitor, evaluate and stop if needed
c10s04.caption: A pilot result is a starting point for a bounded expansion decision, not a universal promise.

c10s05.title: A responsible decision
items: Fair access, autonomy and acceptable burdens
c10s05.caption: The result and the ethical judgment belong in the same decision.
